
Filed from outside audit pass 3 (contrib/claude_fable/reviews/audit_pass3_issue_scoping_2026_11.md, job P3-01; every line below was re-checked at main 34565f3). Covers: pass1 F5. Other jobs from this audit are named here by their P3 key; the Board adds their issue numbers when it files them.

**Why.** A missing ship file turns into a plain block with no error (godot/render/ship_view.gd). The real ship files live only on Ryan's PC. On Nov 9 a capture run pushed with nothing real on screen for this reason (issue 281 run 6). The outside check of the audits asked for this half to be named first in pass 3: it is small and every later capture job leans on it.

**Start from (re-checked at 34565f3).**
- godot/render/ship_view.gd:117 (the plain block fallback) and :30 to :35 (manifest() returns an empty table when res://gen/manifest.json is missing). The file has no push_error, push_warning or printerr at the pin (0 hits).
- godot/.gitignore lines 2 and 5 (gen/ and assets/ships/*/ are out of git by design).
- tools/pc/work_issue.bat:69 (fresh clone; no step copies or builds ship files).
- tools/pc/jobs/bench207_scene_gate.bat:34 (the one existing copy step, a robocopy from build\godot\assets\ships).
- godot/assets/ships/manifest.json (36 ships; every file has bytes and sha256).
- godot/fx/test/vent_look_probe.gd:161 (an existing "if not sv.a4" placeholder test to copy).
- Counted at the pin: 26 files named *_probe.gd or *_shots.gd under godot/. Use one shared helper so each script change is one line.

**What to do.**
- ship_view.gd: when it falls back to the block, print one error line with the hull code and raise a static counter. Do not change what is drawn.
- One helper: "stop if any placeholder" (reads the counter, prints the codes, quits with a non-zero exit code). Call it from every script that saves pictures or measures a scene, before the first picture is written.
- get_ship_files.bat: source folder as the first argument, with a default; copy only, never delete; verify sha256 against the manifest; non-zero exit on any missing or wrong file. Call it from work_issue.bat before the agent starts, and say in the task text where the hulls came from.
- Prove both ways on the PC and paste the two outputs in the report.

**Done test, restated.** A missing hull prints one error line naming the hull and is counted; every capture, probe, shot and bench script exits non-zero with "placeholder hull: <code>" and writes no picture when any ship on screen is a placeholder (proved by running one capture script on a fresh clone with no hulls: non-zero exit, no image; and with hulls copied in: pass); tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat copies godot\gen and godot\assets\ships from a named source folder (copy only), checks every file against the sha256 values in godot/assets/ships/manifest.json and exits non-zero with the list of mismatches; the game itself and GitHub's checks still run without hulls (the stop is for capture runs only); Ryan sees nothing new in the game, and never again gets a sheet of grey blocks.

**What Ryan will see.** Nothing changes on screen. A capture run with no ship files now stops and says "placeholder hull" instead of sending pictures of blocks.

**Size (agent runs and review rounds, from the board's own history; no hours).** 1 workhorse run (history: issue 246 took 20 minutes, issue 26 took 38, issue 335 one run), 1 Board review round, 0 owner rounds. What drives it: the number of scripts to touch (26) and one fresh-clone proof on the PC.

**Waits on.** Nothing. Can run beside a tree job (no shared files) and beside P3-02.

**Risk if done badly.** If the stop is too eager the game or GitHub's parity run stops wherever hulls are absent (GitHub has none). If it is too weak, a scene with some hulls missing still passes. A copy step that deletes or mirrors could remove files on Ryan's PC: copy only.

**Standing rules for this job (FINDINGS R155, R157 and R160; binding).**
1. Fixture state comes from the real functions. A check never types a run, a battle, a pick list or a page state by hand: it makes them with the game's own functions (lineagePick, newRun, startBattle, the real save and load path, the bot).
2. Name every copy you refresh. If you change data.js, battle.js or core.js, re-copy both oracle folders (godot/rules/test/oracle and godot/campaign/test/oracle) and re-export both tables (godot/rules/data/tables.json and godot/campaign/data/campaign_tables.json), run contrib/opus/tools/oracle_copy_test.js last, and list each copy in your report. If the oracle folders no longer exist (job P3-11), re-export the two tables and say so.
3. A behaviour check proves the effect itself (the number moved, the file was refused, the puff sits on the hull). A counter, a callout or the word PASS is not proof. Where the done test says "fails on main first", paste that failing output.
4. Battle camera first for anything visual: judge at the default camera (godot/render/camera_rig.gd, r 170) at true pixel size before any close-up. Views nearer than the game allows (min_r 26) are build checks only.
5. Scope: touch only the folders the Deliver to line lists. Restore any other changed tracked file before you finish. Never commit ship assets, godot/gen or .uid files. Every baked picture keeps its bake script in the repo. Do not push changes to .github/workflows from the PC; deliver them as a patch file and name it.
6. Never write fix, fixes, close, closes, resolve or resolves in front of an issue number in a commit or in the pull request text; write Refs. Plain ASCII, no em dashes, no human-hour estimates. Run the R129 self-check list (callers, saves, twins, UI, which checks GitHub runs).
